research_goal: Identify every independent direct drug member of the mycophenolic-acid Chemical group whose own annotation explicitly identifies its prodrug active form, preserving salt entries and D-to-D identity.
structural_upgrade: Observed basic member-expansion dependency and an entry-level identity boundary. No structural superiority or increased difficulty relative to the specified old tasks has been established.

cg.instruction:
Identify every drug entry in the mycophenolic-acid chemical drug group whose own annotation names the active drug form produced from that prodrug. Return all qualifying drug-ID pairs.

Use the records observed on 12 September 2026. Scope is limited to the direct drug entries in the complete Member field of DG00739, the mycophenolic-acid group with Type Chemical.

1. Read the group's complete Member field to establish the candidate entries.
2. Read each member's complete drug record. Include a member only if its own Comment field explicitly states "Active form of prodrug:" and identifies the active form with a drug reference, "[DR:D...]". Record the member's D identifier as PRODRUG_D and each explicitly linked active-form D identifier as ACTIVE_D.
3. Verify each linked identifier against its drug record.

Keep distinct salt-form drug entries separate, even when names or products overlap. Group membership and group-level Prodrugs links do not establish an entry's own relation. Use drug identifiers (D...); compound identifiers (C...) and group identifiers (DG...) cannot replace them.

A fully read record without the required annotation is excluded only from this documented-relation query; this does not establish that the drug is biologically not a prodrug. An unavailable or incomplete required record leaves the result unresolved and must not be treated as an exclusion or an empty result.
cg.output_format: Return only pipe-separated text. For a nonempty result, use the header PRODRUG_D|ACTIVE_D and one row per distinct ordered pair of drug identifiers. Include every qualifying pair, including every explicitly linked active form when a member has more than one. Remove duplicate pairs. Sort by PRODRUG_D in ascending string order, then by ACTIVE_D in ascending string order. If the fully verified result is empty, return only NONE, without a header. Add no prose or code fences.
